name: bm-v5-porosity-bundling
title: Network porosity & strand bundling
claim: Of the two geometric readouts the model should reproduce, one is met and one is not. The simulated pore-size distribution reaches the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at realistic density, while the protomers-per-strand distribution stays near 1, below the measured 5-7. The released NC1/7S topology has no lateral-association bond, so it cannot form multi-protomer strands — a limitation identified in advance.
experiment: Assemble the real LAMMPS collagen IV network at several densities, then read porosity (pore-size distribution via the maximal-inscribed-disc / distance- transform method) and bundling (protomers per laterally-associated strand, at the measured 59.5 nm cell-deposited lateral spacing) off the snapshot, and place both against the measured comparators.
result: With the parameters corrected to the released code (a 3σ rod, σ≈125 nm), the pore median falls with coverage and lands near or within the measured corneal-EM band (72 ± 40 nm) at the densest network (median ~54 nm): the open mesh is realistic, and pore size is a density knob rather than a fixed property. Bundling stays near 1 (mean ~1.29 protomers per strand, mostly singletons, up to ~6). With no lateral-association bond, the NC1/7S topology cannot build the 5-7-protomer strands measured in the PFHR-9 scaffold.

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition: Diagnostic readout study; gates nothing. Motivates a v2 lateral-association bond.

question: Does the v1 network reproduce the measured pore-size and bundling of a real BM?

purpose.question: Does the v1 network reproduce the measured pore-size and bundling of a real BM?
purpose.mechanism: Porosity is set by the areal density of rods (an emergent mesh); bundling requires lateral association of 5–7 protomers into a strand, a bond the released NC1/7S model does not have (it can bundle only through 7S branching).
purpose.expected_outcome: Pore size tunable into the EM band with density; bundling under-shoots 5–7 because there is no lateral-association bond — a readout that reproduces porosity but exposes a missing connectivity mode.

key_assumptions: Pore size = diameter of the maximal empty disc inscribed in the periodic network plane.
A strand = connected component of rods within 59.5 nm (≈0.5 a) lateral spacing AND near-parallel (≤22°).
Length unit a = 114 nm (bead spacing); readouts converted to nm via a.
Same clean-room parameters and force-independent off-rate as stage 1.

limitations: Cross-check: pore sizes in nm use the wrong length mapping (rod is 1σ here, 3σ in the released code → σ≈125 nm), and bundling is affected by the absent 7S angles that organise trimers. Not a like-for-like comparison.
Clean-room parameters transcribed from the spec; the authors' LAMMPS input scripts are now public (Zenodo 10.5281/zenodo.20719515) and not yet cross-checked against this build.
Bundling is inferred geometrically (lateral proximity + parallelism), not from explicit lateral bonds the model lacks.
Pore sizes depend on the chosen density; the comparator is matched at one coverage, not proven universal.
Single seed per density rung; a seed ensemble would put CIs on the pore/bundling trends.
Same LJ-unit / energy-scale caveat as stage 1 (lengths are firm via a = 114 nm; stiffness is not).

report.title: Stage v5 — porosity & bundling: the geometric readouts
report.verdict: The network reproduces the measured pore-size distribution at realistic density but does not bundle: protomers-per-strand stays near 1, below the measured 5–7. Porosity meets its comparator; bundling identifies a missing lateral-association bond as the next model addition.
report.main_insight: Of the two geometric readouts, porosity falls within the measured band and bundling does not. The gap isolates one missing interaction — a lateral- association bond — rather than a diffuse discrepancy.

sources.note: Corneal BM pore diameter 72 ± 40 nm (low-voltage SEM) — the porosity comparator.
5–7 protomers per laterally-bundled strand in the PFHR-9 scaffold — the bundling comparator.
